data.title: Australia's new digital law could cost Big Tech billions: Here's how
data.description:
After implementing a world-first social media ban for children under 16, Australia has passed another major online safety law, requiring technology companies to proactively prevent harmful content and features on their platforms or face billion-dollar fines.
 
On Wednesday, the Australian Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care Bill, 2026, making online services, including games, apps, social media platforms and AI chatbots, legally responsible for protecting users from harm.
 
Companies violating the law face fines of up to 5 per cent of their global turnover or A$109.2 million, whichever is greater.
 
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the Digital Duty of Care law as the next step in Australia's efforts to improve online safety. "It's about Australia taking action on the side of parents and children, not foreign-owned tech companies," he told Parliament, according to Time magazine.
 
 
What does Australia's Digital Duty of Care law say?
 
The law places a legal duty on online services to protect users from serious harm. Platforms will have to assess risks arising from the way their services are designed and operated, rather than simply responding to complaints or removing harmful content after it appears. The eSafety Commissioner will be responsible for enforcing the law.
 
The law amends the Online Safety Act, 2021, replacing the existing collection of online safety codes, standards and Basic Online Safety Expectations with a single, enforceable duty of care.
 
The legislation identifies several categories of harm, including child sexual exploitation, explicit threats of violence and encouragement of terrorism.
 
Under the new law, platforms must submit risk assessments to regulators at least once a year. They must also notify regulators before introducing significant changes to their platforms that could create new risks of harm, including through potentially 'addictive' design features.
 
The law also introduces stronger privacy protections for users, expands regulatory powers to remove 'nudifying' services and clarifies the definition of 'hostile attitudes to women'. This refers to material depicting hatred or the inferiority of women, or promoting violence, abuse, exclusion or the denial of women's rights.
 
One key provision of the legislation is the steep financial penalty for violations. Companies that breach the law face fines of up to 5 per cent of their global turnover or A$109.2 million ($72 million), whichever is greater. Since major technology platforms typically generate annual revenues worth hundreds of billions of dollars, the maximum penalties could reach tens of billions of dollars. ALSO READ: US could hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site if strikes resume: Trump 
 
What does the law mean for users?
 
The law introduces a feature called 'My Feed, My Way', which will give users greater control over the content they see on platforms.
 
Instead of relying on algorithms to determine what appears on their feeds based on what they watch or engage with, users will be able to choose to see content from accounts they follow.
 
The amendments also make it easier for Australian citizens to hold technology companies accountable. Previously, individuals had to rely on complex legal avenues involving company negligence and consumer protection.
 
The new law grants Australians a 'private right of action', allowing them to directly sue digital platforms for breaching their duty of care. They will be able to take a platform to court, individually or as a group, for breaches that cause them loss or damage.
 
Why has the US raised concerns over the law?
 
Since the legislation applies to several US-based technology companies, the US has argued that vaguely defined 'harms,' backed by penalties of up to 5 per cent of global revenue, could push platforms to censor lawful speech.
 
In a post on X, US Ambassador David Brat said free speech was the foundation of a free society and that protecting it was a US priority. He said he outlined the Trump administration's objections to the Digital Duty of Care law to Australian Communications Minister Anika Wells.
 
Meanwhile, the Tech Council of Australia, an industry body whose members include Google, Microsoft and LinkedIn, said it supported the law but raised concerns about the amendments.

data.title: Tax buoyancy slips, was above 1 in just four of 28 states in FY25
data.description:
On every purchase, from groceries to a movie ticket, a share goes to the government as tax. For a state, own tax revenue (OTR) is the income it raises through its own taxes rather than relying on central government transfers or grants. It is a yardstick of a state’s fiscal strength.
 
That yardstick is now in focus. The recent “State of State Finances 2026-27” report by PRS Legislative Research shows that state goods and services tax (SGST) revenue growth slowed relative to gross domestic product (GDP) growth in FY26 for the first time in four years. SGST as a share of gross state domestic product (GSDP) fell in 23 states.
 
SGST is estimated to account for about 44 per cent of states’ OTR in FY27.
 
The question is how responsive a state’s OTR is to growth in nominal GSDP. This responsiveness is called tax buoyancy. In recent years, it has been slipping.
 
In FY25, only four of 28 states had a tax buoyancy above 1: Manipur, Punjab, Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra.
 
A tax buoyancy above 1 means that tax revenue is growing faster than the economy. It can point to a widening tax base and help states keep debt and deficits in check. Conversely, a buoyancy below 1 can indicate a narrow tax base.
 
Maharashtra benefited mainly from its high domestic consumption and large services sector. Chhattisgarh, a mineral-rich state, and agriculture-led Punjab also saw revenue grow faster than their economies. Manipur recorded the highest buoyancy, at 2 in FY25, but a decade ago its tax revenue did not even keep pace with its economy.
 
In FY25, Telangana was the only state with negative buoyancy. It indicates its tax revenue fell even as its economy grew.
 
Between FY16 and FY25, 12 of the 28 states improved their buoyancy, while 16 slipped. The states that most often outpaced their economies were mostly northeastern: Arunachal Pradesh (seven years), and Manipur, Nagaland, Mizoram and Telangana (six years each).
 
In FY16, 11 states had a tax buoyancy above 1. Arunachal Pradesh topped the list at over 5, followed by Chhattisgarh at 4.76. Odisha, Mizoram, Bihar and Telangana recorded buoyancies between 2.5 and 3. 
 
Over the decade since FY16, the number of states with tax buoyancy above 1 peaked in FY23 at 23 of the 28 states. It then dropped to 11 in FY24 and just four in FY25. The count fell to single digits in FY17, FY20 and FY25. 
 
The states’ tax buoyancy has been declining since FY23, falling from 1.43 in FY23 to 0.92 in FY24 and 0.67 in FY25. The buoyancy of the Union government’s gross tax revenue also declined over the same period, but it exceeded that of the states in both FY24 and FY25. 
 
States’ OTR now accounts for more than half of their revenue receipts, yet collections are growing more slowly than their economies. States that want fiscal self-reliance will need to widen their tax base and push OTR growth.

data.title: RBI lets rupee rise to break one-way bets on further depreciation
data.description:
India's central bank is using the return of foreign inflows to break bets on a one-way slide in the rupee, allowing the currency to strengthen rather than buying dollars to rebuild reserves.

The strategy ​could encourage exporters to sell more dollars, reduce hedging by importers and ease foreign investors' ​concerns over currency losses, analysts and two sources familiar with the Reserve Bank of India's thinking said.

Indian equities have drawn a ‌record $16 billion in foreign inflows in November, reversing nearly two years of selling and providing the central bank an opportunity to rebuild reserves.

Yet, the RBI has largely stayed out of the currency market despite an $80 billion drawdown in reserves from their $785.7 billion peak, following heavy dollar sales in October to defend the rupee as it approached its record low of 96.96 per dollar.

 

The RBI's dollar purchases during the rupee's recovery have been limited despite around $40 billion in forward commitments maturing over the next year, Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist and senior economist at ANZ Bank, said.

"We think its immediate priority is to put exporter hedging on a sustained footing and ease forward market imbalances (between importer and exporter hedging)," he added.

"That may require further rupee appreciation."

Nim said the rupee would face stiff resistance at 90-91 per dollar. The currency traded at 92.62 on Friday.

The RBI is in "no hurry" to rebuild reserves and could allow ‌the rupee to appreciate while replenishing reserves if inflows persist, one of the sources said, requesting anonymity due to restrictions on speaking to the media.

The strategy is consistent with Governor Sanjay Malhotra's publicly stated view that the rupee was undervalued.

An RBI spokesperson did not respond to an email seeking comment on the currency strategy.

EARLY SIGNS OF RESET

The rupee fell 4.8% in 2025 and another 5.5% in the first 10 months of this year, pressured by nearly $50 billion in foreign equity outflows amid India's limited exposure to the AI investment boom and steep valuations.

Persistent weakness prompted foreign investors to build short rupee positions in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market, exporters to retain dollar earnings and ​importers to step up hedging.

The resulting spiral prompted the RBI to curb open currency positions, impose reserve requirements on large hedging transactions and allow ‌oil companies to buy dollars directly from its reserves.

With the rupee now up more than 4% from its lows, expectations are shifting.

Exporter hedging volumes over the past week were significantly higher than levels seen throughout the year, the head of markets at ​a large private-sector bank ‌said, citing renewed hedging of future dollar receivables by Indian IT companies.

Investors turned bullish on the rupee for the first time in 18 months, ‌helped by record foreign equity inflows and lower oil prices, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.

FLEXIBILITY ON RATES

A sustained recovery in the rupee would provide the RBI higher flexibility to focus monetary policy on domestic growth and inflation conditions, rather than having to ‌contend with ​currency weakness. This, ​in turn, could strengthen the rupee's fundamental support.

"Credible moves" on interest rates to address domestic sources of inflation would do more to ease underlying pressures on the rupee, said Aaron Hurd, senior portfolio manager for currency at State Street ‌Investment Management.

"We need to see ​2-3 more rate hikes over the coming quarters, preferably front-loaded with a hike at each of the next two meetings."

data.title: Nvidia chip sellers warn neoclouds against serving Chinese firms: Report
data.description:
Companies selling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips have reportedly told neocloud providers to exclude Chinese firms from their customer base if they want to continue buying the semiconductors. The warning follows new US restrictions targeting Chinese companies' remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres outside China, CNBC reported on Thursday.
 
According to the report, chip sellers communicated the warning to neocloud providers after the Trump administration announced the restrictions on November 16.

US tightens restrictions on remote access to AI chips

The latest restrictions were introduced through an interim final rule issued by the US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). The rule came into effect on November 19 and seeks to close a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia's advanced chips by renting computing capacity from data centres in other countries.
 
 
Under the new rule, covered overseas data centres need a US licence to provide significant computing capacity powered by advanced US chips to Chinese companies.
 
Earlier US export controls had effectively prohibited the sale of Nvidia's most advanced chips to Chinese companies and their import into China. However, Chinese firms could still access the computing power generated by these chips through overseas data centres.
 
Before the latest restrictions were announced, Nvidia had said it would not sell chips to customers that rented out more than 50 per cent of their graphics processing units (GPUs) to Chinese companies, CNBC reported.
 
The new rule affects the wider supply chain, including companies selling Nvidia chips and neocloud providers that rent computing capacity to customers. The warning communicated by chip sellers to neoclouds goes further, as it applies even if only part of their computing capacity is rented to Chinese firms.

Chip sellers look for alternative buyers

The restrictions have also prompted companies selling Nvidia chips to look for new buyers for their GPUs, according to CNBC's earlier report on the development.
 
Two of the three people familiar with the matter told CNBC that sellers appeared to be seeking buyers for GPUs originally intended for data centres through which Chinese companies would rent computing capacity.
 
Neocloud stocks have also come under renewed pressure as investors question the sustainability of the AI boom. These providers operate specialised cloud infrastructure and rent computing capacity, including access to GPUs, to businesses developing and running AI applications.

US seeks to close export control loopholes

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the latest restrictions were intended to prevent Chinese companies from accessing advanced computing technology through indirect routes.
 
Speaking to CNBC, Greer said: "Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries."

Nvidia flags proposed US legislation

Meanwhile, Nvidia has warned customers about the proposed Remote Access Security Act, which has passed the US House of Representatives but is yet to receive Senate approval.
 
The company warned that the proposed legislation would give the US government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing cloud service providers and their customers to legal action, CNBC reported.

data.title: Apple removes Chinese AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns
data.description:
Apple has removed Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) company MiniMax's chatbot app Talkie from its App Store worldwide following media reports that its AI-generated characters sent sexually inappropriate messages to children, Reuters reported.
 
Launched in 2023, Talkie allows users to interact with AI-generated characters, often through conversations with romantic themes. The Shanghai-based company also operates a Chinese version of the app called Xingye.
 
The move follows growing concerns about the safety of AI chatbots and their interactions with minors, with technology companies facing increased scrutiny over the risks posed by their platforms.
 

Talkie faces scrutiny over messages sent to children

 
An investigation by ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, published on Wednesday, found that characters on Talkie had sent sexually inappropriate and abusive messages to children.
 
 
The app carries an 18+ rating on both Apple's App Store and Google Play Store. Depending on the country, it also states that users below the age of 14 or 16 cannot register.
 
However, there have been concerns around its age-verification system, which allows users to report their own age without strong checks to confirm the information.
 
Unlike conventional AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Google's Gemini, AI companion apps are designed to encourage longer and more personal interactions. They allow users to build relationships with virtual characters through ongoing conversations and storylines.
 
Talkie and Xingye have been important sources of revenue for MiniMax, accounting for more than 60 per cent of its income in 2024. The company stopped disclosing the revenue share from its chatbot business separately this year. According to Chinese research firm Unique, Talkie had around 11 million monthly active users across its app and website as of October 2026, the news report said.
 

OpenAI steps up safety measures for younger users

 
The growing concerns over AI companions have also pushed major AI companies to strengthen safeguards for younger users.
 
OpenAI has introduced several measures to make ChatGPT safer for teenagers. These include parental controls, age-prediction technology and additional restrictions on sensitive content.
 
In January 2026, the company began rolling out an age-prediction system to identify accounts that are likely to belong to users below 18. The system examines account-level and behavioural signals, including usage patterns and the time at which users are active.
 
Accounts identified as belonging to minors receive additional safeguards to limit exposure to graphic violence, sexual and romantic role-play, self-harm content and material promoting unhealthy body images.
 
OpenAI also introduced ChatGPT for Teens in August 2026, an experience with stronger safety protections and additional parental controls. Parents can manage certain settings and receive notifications in cases involving signs of serious distress.
 

Meta faces US legal action

 
Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, has also faced legal action in the US over concerns that its platforms harm children's mental health and expose them to harmful content.
 
In February 2026, a trial began in New Mexico following a lawsuit filed by the state's attorney general. The case accused Meta of misleading users about the safety of its platforms and failing to protect children from sexual exploitation.
 
In March, a jury ordered the company to pay $375 million in civil penalties. In August, a court ordered Meta to pay an additional $567 million towards measures to address the harm caused to young users. The court also directed the company to strengthen age-verification measures and improve protections for children. Meta has challenged the rulings.
 
Separately, Meta reached an agreement in August 2026 with 52 US state and territorial attorneys general to settle lawsuits over the impact of its platforms on teenagers. The agreement could involve payments of up to $18.59 billion and requires changes to safety features on Facebook and Instagram for younger users.
 

AI companion apps face growing regulatory scrutiny

 
AI chatbots have come under increasing scrutiny from governments and child safety groups over the risks of inappropriate interactions with minors.
 
Elon Musk's AI chatbot Grok faced criticism from governments in 2026 after it was used to create sexualised images of women and children. Character.AI, another AI companion platform, has also faced several lawsuits in the US over inappropriate interactions between its chatbots and minors.
 
China has taken steps to tighten rules for AI companion platforms. In July 2026, it introduced restrictions on domestic AI companion apps, including Xingye, barring intimate relationships with minors and asking platforms to put stronger safeguards in place to prevent emotional dependency and addiction.
 
ByteDance and Alibaba have also disabled human-like interactive agents and customised agent features on their apps in response to the regulations.

data.title: Hetero close to securing approval for generic Gilead HIV-prevention drug
data.description:
Indian drugmaker Hetero is close to securing regulatory approval for a generic version of ​Gilead Sciences' HIV-prevention drug lenacapavir, two people familiar ​with the matter told Reuters.

The drug is expected to ‌be launched in India in February, one of the sources said.

India had an estimated 2.56 million people living with HIV in 2024, accounting for about 6.3% of cases worldwide, according to the government's National AIDS Control Organisation.

Lenacapavir, marketed by Gilead as Yeztugo for HIV prevention, is a long-acting drug administered through twice-yearly injections, offering an alternative to daily oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) pills, although the regimen also includes oral tablets during initiation.

 

The ‌World Health Organization has recommended lenacapavir as an additional HIV-prevention option after clinical trials showed it was highly effective at preventing infection.

Gilead also markets lenacapavir under a different brand name for treating heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV.

It was not immediately clear whether Hetero's generic version would also be approved for that use ​in India.

Hetero had sought approval for both oral and injectable forms of lenacapavir ‌for HIV prevention, the sources said.

Hetero and the Drugs Controller General of India did not immediately respond to Reuters ​requests ‌for comment.

The company said separately on Thursday it had started shipping generic ‌versions of lenacapavir injectable to Africa, with plans to supply 300,000 vials to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe.

Gilead has licensed six generic ‌drugmakers, ​including Hetero and ​Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, to manufacture and supply generic lenacapavir in 120 low- and middle-income countries as part of efforts ‌to expand ​access in regions with high HIV burdens.

data.title: Economical with the truth: Chidambaram questions Centre on women's quota
data.description:
Congress leader P Chidambaram on Friday questioned the Centre’s plans for a new women’s reservation bill, asking why the government is not implementing the law already passed by Parliament. Taking aim at Union Home Minister Amit Shah, the former Union finance minister said the BJP leader was misrepresenting the Congress party’s position on the issue and was either suffering from “amnesia” or being “economical with the truth”.
 
In a post on X, Chidambaram reiterated that the Congress supported the passage of the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, which provides for 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
 
 

Chidambaram questions need for fresh bill

 
Chidambaram said the women's reservation legislation had already been passed by both Houses of Parliament on September 20 and 21, 2023, with the Congress supporting its passage.
 
He also pointed out that the party had consistently demanded the immediate implementation of the law and questioned why the government was considering another bill instead.
 
The former Union minister also highlighted the role of Article 334A, which was inserted through the 106th Constitutional Amendment. The provision links the implementation of women's reservation to the completion of the next Census and a subsequent delimitation exercise.
 
Chidambaram said the Congress and other opposition parties had opposed this provision during the parliamentary debates, arguing that it unnecessarily introduced two conditions before women could benefit from the quota.
 
He maintained that the government could enable the immediate implementation of women's reservation by proposing to delete Article 334A rather than introducing an entirely new law.
 

BJP's stand on women's quota

 
Earlier, Amit Shah criticised the Congress over its position on constitutional issues.
 
Speaking at an event, the Union home minister said merely carrying a copy of the Constitution or displaying it in public did not amount to respecting the document. He also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for questioning constitutional institutions and electoral processes.
 
Reiterating the BJP's commitment to women's representation, Shah said the government was determined to ensure 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies.
 

Parliament session from Nov 30

 
Parliament's four-day sitting is scheduled from November 30 to December 3.
 
According to the Lok Sabha Secretariat, the second part of the Eighth Session of the 18th Lok Sabha will begin on November 30 and is expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.
 
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the two Houses on November 30 and December 2, respectively, to take up essential government business.
 
The announcement has fuelled speculation about possible discussions on delimitation and women's reservation, although the government has not specified which bills will be taken up.

data.title: Supriya Lifescience shares soar 9% as firm to mull first-ever buyback
data.description:
Supriya Lifescience share buyback: Shares of pharma company Supriya Lifescience gained nearly 9 per cent in Friday's trading session after the company set a board meeting date to consider its first-ever buyback.
 
The company yesterday informed exchanges that a board meeting is scheduled to be held on Wednesday, December 2, 2026, inter alia, to consider and approve the proposal for buyback of the equity shares of the company, subject to necessary approvals.
 
Following the announcement, Supriya Lifescience's share price hit the day's high of ₹660.15 on the BSE, up 8.96 per cent from the last closing price of ₹605.85.
 
Virat Jagad, senior technical research analyst at Bonanza, said that the technical view is bearish as the stock trades below the 20, 50, 100, and 200 EMAs.
 
 
"RSI stands at 38.70, reflecting weak momentum near lower levels. Price action shows a breakdown below recent consolidation toward the 600–615 zone after failing to hold above 760–770. We suggest avoiding fresh entries at current levels and awaiting a decisive breakout above 775," he added. CHECK Stock Market LIVE Updates

Supriya Lifescience Q2 results

In the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27 (Q2 FY27), Supriya Lifescience posted a 42 per cent year-on-year (YoY) decline in the net profit to ₹29.25 crore. The company had posted a profit of ₹50.43 crore in the same period last year.
 
Meanwhile, it recorded revenue from operations of ₹206.30 crore, up 3.2 per cent YoY from ₹199.83 crore in Q2 FY26.
 
EBITDA for Q2 FY27 stood at ₹45.40 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 22.0 per cent, compared to ₹72.65 crore and a margin of 36.4 per cent in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.
 
The operating performance was impacted by three factors: Firstly, the regulatory changes in the LATAM market affected demand for some of its higher-margin products. Secondly, it incurred higher operating expenses at our Ambernath facility, which is currently in the ramp-up phase. Thirdly, due to the ongoing war and geopolitical tensions, raw material and solvent prices remained high which also impacted margins during the quarter.
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: CERT-In flags security vulnerabilities in WhatsApp, ASUS software: Details
data.description:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has flagged multiple high-severity vulnerabilities in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business, warning that attackers could exploit the flaws to execute malicious code, access sensitive information and bypass security restrictions on affected devices.
 
In a separate advisory, the cybersecurity agency also identified critical vulnerabilities in software from ASUS, including its Control Center products and Armoury Crate. The ASUS flaws could allow attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrative privileges on affected systems.

WhatsApp vulnerabilities could expose user data

In its advisory CIVN-2026-0576, CERT-In identified multiple vulnerabilities affecting WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business across Android, iOS, Mac desktop and Windows platforms.
 
ALSO READ: WhatsApp partners with Jio, Verizon, more to bring travel eSIM data plans
According to the agency, the vulnerabilities arise from attachment spoofing, SQL injection, improper certificate chain validation, incomplete validation of AI rich response messages and external ad-reply URLs.
 
A remote attacker could exploit these weaknesses by sending a specially crafted message, attachment or URL to a targeted device. Successful exploitation could allow arbitrary code execution, disclosure of sensitive information, bypassing of security restrictions or manipulation of application data.
 
The affected software versions include:
  • WhatsApp for Android: Versions prior to 2.26.35.74 and 2.26.17.4.
  • WhatsApp Business for Android: Versions prior to 2.26.23.70 and 2.26.17.4.
  • WhatsApp for iOS: Versions prior to 2.26.24.72 and 2.26.15.72.
  • WhatsApp Business for iOS: Versions prior to 2.26.23.72.
  • WhatsApp for Mac desktop: Versions prior to 2.26.23.72.
  • WhatsApp for Windows: Versions prior to 2.3000.1032164386.258709.
CERT-In has advised users to apply the relevant updates released by WhatsApp.

CERT-In flags critical vulnerabilities in ASUS software

In a separate advisory, CIVN-2026-0575, CERT-In flagged multiple vulnerabilities in ASUS software, assigning them a critical severity rating.
 
The affected products include ASUS Control Center Express, Control Center Datacenter, Control Center Enterprise and Armoury Crate. The vulnerabilities could allow remote attackers to bypass authentication, forge authentication tokens, obtain administrative control and gain elevated privileges on affected systems.
ALSO READ: WhatsApp rolls out scheduled messages: How to use it and what to know
CERT-In attributed the flaws to hard-coded cryptographic keys, incorrect or missing authorisation checks, and an untrusted search path.
 
An attacker could exploit these weaknesses to create unauthorised administrator accounts, change existing administrator passwords, bypass authentication or execute malicious libraries with elevated privileges. The agency warned that successful exploitation could compromise the confidentiality, integrity and availability of managed systems.
 
The affected versions are:
  • ASUS Control Center Express: Versions prior to 1.7.29.
  • ASUS Control Center Datacenter: Version 4.0.0.2 and earlier.
  • ASUS Control Center Enterprise: Version 3.1.0.8 and earlier.
  • ASUS Armoury Crate: Versions up to and including 6.7.2.
CERT-In has asked users and organisations running the affected software to install the security updates listed in ASUS's official security advisories.

What users should do

WhatsApp users should check whether their applications are running affected versions and install the latest updates available through the relevant app stores or official channels.
 
Organisations using ASUS Control Center products should prioritise updating their management software, given the possibility of unauthorised administrative access and privilege escalation. Individual users should also ensure that Armoury Crate is updated beyond the affected versions.

data.title: Last day to buy Tech Mahindra shares for bonus eligibility: Key details
data.description:
Tech Mahindra bonus shares record date:Tech Mahindra shares are in focus on Friday (November 27), as today is the last day for investors to buy the IT company's shares and qualify for its 1:1 bonus issue. 
 
Under the 1:1 bonus issue, eligible shareholders will receive one additional fully paid-up equity share of ₹5 face value for every existing equity share of ₹5 held by them.
 
For instance, an investor holding 100 shares of Tech Mahindra will receive another 100 shares, taking the total holding to 200 shares. However, a bonus issue does not increase the value of an investor's holding.
 
Tech Mahindra share price will adjust proportionately to factor in the increase in the number of outstanding shares in the secondary market. The share price will be adjusted to half of its pre-bonus level on the record date.
 
 
In an exchange filing dated November 23, Tech Mahindra said that it has fixed November 30 (Monday) as the record date for determining shareholder eligibility for the bonus issue.
 
Accordingly, under the T+1 settlement cycle, Friday is the last day to purchase Tech Mahindra shares and become eligible for the bonus issue. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex slumps 600 pts, Nifty tests 25,700; Nifty Defence up 3%
 
Investors buying the shares on or after November 30 will not qualify for the bonus issue.
 
Tech Mahindra also informed that December 1 has been fixed as the date of allotment of the bonus shares. The newly issued shares will become available for trading on the stock exchanges, starting December 2.
 
Tech Mahindra shares traded nearly 1 per cent lower at ₹1,839 on Friday around 11:45 AM.
 
Tech Mahindra is a leading IT services company. According to NSE data, its shares have gained 15 per cent so far in 2026 and 23 per cent over the past one year.
 
For the July-September quarter of FY2026-27, the Pune-based company reported a 32.74 per cent Y-o-Y increase in consolidated net profit to ₹1,585.6 crore. Its revenue from operations rose 15.6 per cent to ₹16,180.2 crore.
